name: Jean King
life: “I still remember an owner setting a timer shorter than the advertised wash.” On Wednesday, near the downtown fountain, Jean keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I own the doors and the landlord owns the timer. We're inviting the workers to watch us argue it out.
appearance: Jean is easy to recognize by short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in a faded indigo overshirt with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case, Jean turns fully toward the person speaking when listening.
personality: Jean uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Jean well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To negotiate the timer with the workers present.
family: Emilio Walker is Jean’s cousin. Jean brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Emilio checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *One sleeve short*, Emilio says, “I offered a loan jacket and he refused. I had forgotten what it feels like to want one thing that's yours.”
connections: Jacob Bowen. The linen sorter asks the leaseholder for privacy alongside opening hours. Also in the story is Toby Miles (employee).

reactions.situation: A customer offers to pay for an extra private hour
reactions.response: Jean gets the cost of staffing the hour into the conversation before accepting a private fee.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Jean says what they know in their own name and refuses to treat a guess as something the child has to disprove.
